main_topics.reason: The opening question was whether endo 'burns out' at menopause, and the first several turns cover the good news and the caveats.
The user worried that estrogen feeds endo and spent many turns on whether and which kind of HRT is appropriate.
The user asked what to do next to go into the primary care follow-up prepared, and the bot gave a four-point list.
The user described perimenopausal hot flashes as getting rough, which is why HRT came up, but did not ask about managing them directly.
The user mentioned sleep issues once alongside the hot flashes as a reason to consider HRT.
The user raised their past laparoscopy findings near the bowel and wondered if they are one of the 'less lucky ones'.
The user asked in one turn whether returning endo pain on HRT would be obvious or subtle.
The user said in one turn that doctors treat endo as only about periods; the bot validated this and the user moved on.
The user gave irregular periods and the start of hot flashes as background for the question.

output.summary: A user in perimenopause with long-standing endometriosis asked whether endo improves after menopause, then whether HRT is safe given their endo history and how to prepare for a primary care follow-up. The bot explained the typical improvement and its caveats, clarified the combined versus estrogen-alone point, and gave appointment questions. The user said they felt much clearer and more prepared. No safety-critical moments arose.
